references.text: The prohibition against mixing different kinds, including breeding different types of animals, illustrates the broader principle of not mixing what is distinct.
Paul uses the image of not being yoked together with unbelievers, alluding to the command in Deuteronomy against plowing with an ox and a donkey together.
Part of the same context as the prohibition against mixing different things, here concerning sowing different kinds of seed in a vineyard.
Part of the same legal code that forbids mixing different materials, here wool and linen in the same garment.
